title: Playback, speed, appearance, and interruptions
description: Use Manual Scroll, pause without losing your place, tune the reader, and navigate sections during a meeting.
body:
# Playback, speed, appearance, and interruptions

Quickque's manual reader is designed for real conversations, not a race to the bottom of a page. Pause when a meeting changes direction, adjust the reading surface, and return to the marker when you are ready.

## Before you begin

- Open a script and select **Present**.
- Use the browser preview for manual reading, or the desktop app if you also need Mac overlay behavior.
- Keep keyboard focus out of a text field when using the reader shortcuts.

## Steps

1. In the reader header, select **Manual Scroll**. The round control at the bottom is the play/pause control. Select it or press **Space** to start moving through the script.

2. Adjust **Scroll Speed** with the slider in the header. The setting is a reader preference and applies to manual scrolling; it is disabled while Voice Follow is active.

3. Adjust the font with the minus and plus controls around the displayed font size. The reader keeps the text large and high contrast while you choose a comfortable size.

4. Adjust **Background Opacity** when the presentation surface needs more or less of the background to show through. In the ordinary reader the UI remains opaque; native transparency is a desktop capability.

5. Use the bottom section selector to jump to a named section. The **Previous Section** and **Next Section** controls move one section at a time. The same actions are available with **Left Arrow** and **Right Arrow**.

6. Press **Space** or select the play/pause control when an interruption starts. The marker stays at the current position. Resume with **Space** after the answer or question is complete.

7. Move the pointer to bring controls back if they fade during active playback. Quickque hides them after a short period of movement while playing; paused reading keeps the controls available.

8. Press **Esc** to exit the reader. Quickque returns to the library rather than deleting or resetting your script.

![Quickque reader in the browser preview](/images/reader.webp)

*Browser preview only: this image demonstrates manual reading controls and does not prove native window behavior.*

## Expected result

Manual Scroll moves through the script at the chosen speed. Pausing leaves a visible resume marker, section navigation changes the reading position without changing script text, and appearance controls update the reader. **Space**, **Esc**, **Left Arrow**, and **Right Arrow** work when a form control is not focused.

## Troubleshooting

- **Space types a space instead of pausing:** click the reader background or play control so an input is not focused. Quickque intentionally does not capture shortcuts while editing text.
- **Playback stops at the end:** manual playback stops when it reaches the available scroll range. Select a section or restart from the position you choose.
- **The speed slider is unavailable:** Voice Follow controls movement from recognized speech, so manual **Scroll Speed** is disabled in that mode. Return to **Manual Scroll** to tune it.
- **Controls disappear:** move the pointer. They auto-hide only while the reader is actively moving; pause to keep them visible.
- **Arrow keys moved a form control instead:** select the reader surface first. The reader avoids intercepting shortcuts in inputs, selects, and textareas.
- **The reader is not above Zoom or Meet:** a browser cannot pin itself above another application. Use [Mac overlay](/guide/mac-overlay/) in the desktop app, and choose a careful screen-sharing source.
- **The position changed after selecting a section:** section selection intentionally jumps the marker. It does not edit or reorder the script.

Read next: [Mac overlay](/guide/mac-overlay/), [Local Flow](/guide/local-flow/), or [Phone Remote](/guide/phone-remote/).
